page: Microsoft Azure D2als_v6 is a general-purpose, low-memory virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Configured with two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core via simultaneous multithreading, the instance provides 4.0 GB of system memory, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. The x86_64 CPU architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512 (f, vnni, and bf16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions.

Hardware integration excludes bundled local storage and dedicated hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs and relying entirely on remote network-attached disks via Azure Premium Storage capabilities. Network allocation does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks reveal strong single-core compute performance, ranking in the top quartile with a Geekbench single-core score of 2022.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 3078.57. However, overall multi-core and throughput metrics reflect the low core count, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 2600.0 and PassMark CPU reaching 3820.57.

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate 37.22 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 27.76 GB/sec for write operations, matching mid-tier throughput profiles. Compression tasks deliver balanced results, including 29.15 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip compression and 13.44 GB/sec for single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In application-level benchmarks, the instance achieves 2.95 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 3.44 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, alongside 100.63 tokens per second for small 135M model LLM text generation.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, lack of ephemeral disks, and entry-level multithreaded capacity, the D2als_v6 delivers a cost-efficient hardware profile for compute workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation and modern vector instruction execution without heavy memory demands. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, continuous integration build agents, and single-threaded background tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure D2als_v6 is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features two dedicated vCPUs across one physical core, 4.0 GB of RAM, 32 MB of L3 cache, and AVX-512 instruction support. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs, relying on remote Premium Storage options. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread execution, placing in the top quartile for Geekbench and stress-ng single-core tests, though multithreaded throughput is constrained by its dual-thread hardware footprint. Memory write speeds and single-threaded compression benchmarks exhibit average performance, while database operations and uncached memory reads show lower relative throughput. The D2als_v6 provides resource efficiency for low-footprint workloads, including microservices, simple web servers, CI/CD runners, and utility processing jobs.
